text:
The Oilers have won six straight and are 17-3-3, and Connor McDavid just broke Wayne Gretzky's Oilers record for power-play points, per Oilersnation. On Tuesday they beat Florida 5-2. It's a great story. By our numbers it is also one built on a lot of luck, and both things can be true.

Edmonton has 37 points against about 26 expected. The Oilers get just over half of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and have scored 24 more goals than those chances earned. During the six-game run they had only 45% of the expected goals, with the goaltending saving 9.4 goals above expected. Tristan Jarry is at .951 over his last five starts, and Devon Levi, the goalie everyone has been writing about since the Sabres let him go, stopped 21 of 23 against Florida.

The good part is real. McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Vasily Podkolzin together have outscored opponents 22-6 with 61% of the expected goals, and Evan Bouchard with Mattias Ekholm has been on for 26 goals for and 5 against. The worry is everything past those five. The Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line sits at 32% and has been outscored 11-5, and the Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea pair is underwater too. Mike Babcock's team is 99% to make the playoffs by our odds. What we'd watch is how the depth holds up when the goalies stop stopping everything.
